title: On Windows a registered focused Vitest run has no classified verification route, so UI-only changes cannot satisfy the committed-input evaluation precondition with their own tests
outcome: A UI change's own Vitest tests, run as a registered `--input commit` focused run on Windows, produce a classified verification record. That lets the committed-input evaluation precondition be met with the change's own tests, not a substitute check.
acceptance: On Windows, a registered focused `--input commit` run of named Vitest test files in ui/ (in a form the launcher accepts) produces a verification record classified as Test, and Engram acknowledges it.
A test covers that classification on the form used; it checks behaviour (the classified kind or the refusal), not source text.
The documented focused form for UI tests on Windows names the supported command.
